info.name: Marlink PRA API v3.2.0
info.description:
# Marlink PRA API v3.2.0

PRA API collection for customers and operators: every approved operation authenticated with an access key. Internal operations (X-API-Key, access management) are not part of it.

Generated from the pra-api source code (package version 3.2.0): 135 operations in 34 controllers. Do not edit it by hand; it is regenerated from code at the end of every iteration.

## One-time setup

1. Import this collection. Optionally import the environment template `marlink-pra-api.postman_environment.json` shipped with pra-api.
2. Create an environment (or use the Postman Vault) and set `baseUrl`, `accessKey` and `tenantId`. Keep secrets in the environment or the vault: the collection variables are exported empty on purpose and must never hold credentials.
3. Set the resource id variables (for example `customerId`, `siteId`) when you need them. They are empty on purpose, so that no request addresses an existing resource by accident.

No access to the Marlink Postman workspace and no Postman API key are needed.

## Base URL

`baseUrl` is the scheme, host and optional path prefix in front of the controller paths, without a trailing slash. The API has no global prefix and no URI versioning (`src/main.ts`).

- Calling the API service directly: use the API host, for example `https://pra-api-pp.cdn-vas.net`. Do not add `/api`.
- Calling through the PRA Console: use `https://<console-host>/api`. The Console forwards `/api` to the API; the OpenAPI document declares this relative server `/api`.

## Authentication

- Default: `X-Access-Key: {{accessKey}}`, configured once on the collection (API Key auth) and inherited by the requests.
- Requests without an authentication guard override it with "No Auth".
- Credentials are never sent to an endpoint that does not read them.

## X-Tenant-Id

`X-Tenant-Id` carries the **BeyondTrust instance id** (see GET /beyondtrust-instances), never a customer id. It is an enabled row where the handler requires it and a disabled row where it only narrows the customer scope. `tenantId` is empty and never defaults to an instance.

## Request conventions

- Required path, query and header inputs are enabled. Optional query parameters and headers are included but disabled; enable them when needed.
- `X-Transaction-Id` is optional wherever the API reads it and disabled by default.
- Array query parameters are sent by repeating the key (`?name=a&name=b`).
- Request bodies hold the minimal valid body (required fields). The saved example "Full body" holds every writable field with representative nested objects and arrays.
- JSON body properties cannot be disabled like query or header rows: remove the optional properties you do not want to send. Each request documents its fields (path, type, required, null accepted, rules).
- PATCH requests change only the fields you send; where an empty object is rejected, the minimal body sends one field.
- All example data is synthetic. Examples are validated locally against the DTO validation rules of the API; they were not executed against an environment. The response part of saved examples is illustrative (status code only).

## Variables

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | Scheme, host and optional path prefix in front of the controller paths, without a trailing slash. API host directly: no /api. Through the PRA Console ingress: https://<console-host>/api. |
| `accessKey` | Access key sent as X-Access-Key. Secret: set it in a local environment or the Postman Vault, never here. |
| `tenantId` | BeyondTrust instance id sent as X-Tenant-Id (GET /beyondtrust-instances). Not a customer id. Intentionally empty, never defaulted. |
| `transactionId` | Optional correlation id for X-Transaction-Id (disabled rows). The API generates one when absent. |
| `backupId` | Id of the backup addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `beyondtrustInstanceId` | Id of the beyondtrust instance addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `customerId` | Id of the customer addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `groupPolicyId` | Id of the group policy addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `groupPolicyMemberId` | Id of the group policy member addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `jumpClientId` | Id of the jump client addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `jumpClientInstallerId` | Id of the jump client installer addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `jumpGroupId` | Id of the jump group addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `jumpointId` | Id of the jumpoint addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `jumpointNodeId` | Id of the jumpoint node addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `jumpPolicyId` | Id of the jump policy addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `protocolTunnelJumpId` | Id of the protocol tunnel jump addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `remoteRdpId` | Id of the remote rdp addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `remoteVncId` | Id of the remote vnc addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `shellJumpId` | Id of the shell jump addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `siteAuditorId` | Id of the site auditor addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `siteId` | Id of the site addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `siteManagerId` | Id of the site manager addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `siteSupportTeamMemberId` | Id of the site support team member addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `teamId` | Id of the team addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `userId` | Id of the user addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |
| `webJumpId` | Id of the web jump addressed by path parameters. Set it before sending; it is intentionally empty. |

## Folders

- **Customers**: Customers (one per business unit and BeyondTrust instance) and their lifecycle.
- **Sites**: Sites of a customer and their manager, auditor, support team and jumpoint assignments.
- **BeyondTrust Instances**: Registered BeyondTrust instances (tenants) and their configuration backups.
- **Users**: BeyondTrust users and their group policy memberships.
- **Teams**: BeyondTrust teams and their members.
- **Group Policies**: Group policies and their members, teams, jump groups and jumpoints.
- **Jump Groups**: Jump groups.
- **Jump Policies**: Jump policies.
- **Jump Clients**: Installed jump clients and jump client installers.
- **Jump Items**: Jump items by type: remote RDP, remote VNC, shell jump, web jump and protocol tunnel jump.
- **Jumpoints**: Jumpoints, their nodes and installers.
- **Session Policies**: Session policies (read only).
- **License Usage**: License usage calculation per customer and per site.
- **SOC**: Consolidated projections for the Security Operations Center integration.
- **Deployments**: Jumpoint node deployments.
- **Health and Platform**: Liveness, readiness, diagnostics and the root endpoints.

request.description:
Retrieve customers.

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | `CustomerController.retrieveCustomers()` in `src/customer/controllers/customer.controller.ts` (module `CustomerModule`) |
| Authentication | X-Access-Key header (`{{accessKey}}`) |
| Swagger | documented in /open-api |
| Customer export | included |

**Authorisation and scope**

- X-Access-Key must match a configured access entry; its business units define the scope.
- The access key must define at least one business unit (403 otherwise).
- Checks that the addressed resource and the filters belong to the business units or customers of the access key (403 otherwise).

**Headers**

| Name | Type | Required | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X-Transaction-Id` | string | no | Optional correlation id for tracing a request across services and logs. Generated by the API when absent. |

Optional headers are present but disabled; enable them when needed.

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pageSize` | integer | no | The number of items to include in a paginated response. Default `100`. |
| `pageNumber` | integer | no | The 1-based index of the desired page. Default `1`. |
| `key` | string | no | Unique key for the customer. |
| `name` | string | no | Unique name of the customer. |
| `businessUnits` | array<enum> | no | Filter customers by business units. Repeat the parameter for several values (`?name=a&name=b`). One of `MT`, `OA`, `MC`, `EG`, `TE`. |

Optional query parameters are present but disabled; enable them when needed.

**Responses**

- 200: `CustomerRetrievedDtoOutput[]`

**Notes**

- Records the request path in the monitoring table.
